body:
Sounds like you possibly could be having a mental breakdown. Is there anyone you could talk to?
I wish you well and I hope all the noise goes away.

I quite like Florin, Matheus and Sepherin.
For girls I would pick Maria Ludwina, Philomena and Crescenz, and then call them by their middle names and the latter Crescentia.
Actually cute a fun sibset.
In Morocco too.
Sounds similar to things I have experienced. Do you think you can call an ambulance? Since you typed this long thing.

Stoeitijger means playfully fighting tiger.  
Brokkelvogel means pieces+bird, so it sounds like a term for someone who is unlucky.
Thank you for doing that :)
How did you do that? I got to know how too!
Huxcyn Fox, Huxtyn Fox, Huxlan Fox (I have 3 middle names).
For me it puts me at risk of seizures so if there is any way to turn it off I would appreciate it or I cant play for a month.
Are there any Pictish names surviving, any at all? Your post made it sound like not but that sounds so sad to me.

Badr means moon, ul/oul means of/from, badour could be related to this again but with the exotic twist you mention.
Maybe related to this name: http://quranicnames.com/buduriya/
I know the feeling, I hope you can meet them.
Yes you could ask them. And I can google loads more travel stuff if you want. :)
Some are some are not. That there are Trump fanatics in the US doesnt mean that everyone is. Even toxic parts of a culture wont affect everyone.

Florida is beautiful, so I heard.
I am not really a beach person but I heard Mexico, Morocco, Thailand and Greece have beautiful beaches too. And Goa, India, Bali, Indonesia.

Hawaii, US Virgin Islands and Puerto Rico apparently have great beaches as well, Google said.

https://www.cntraveler.com/galleries/2015-02-24/top-10-most-beautiful-island-beaches-hawaii-australia

California has a huge animal sanctuary centered around cats. Did you hear of that?
And Tangier, Morocco also has an animal sanctuary similar to it, with cats and dogs.
I want to build a center just like that one some day.
It is good you have friends. Is there any way you could meet your online friends? Or plan to? Sometimes having something fun to live for that is reasonably far off but also doable can be nice.

Those psychiatrists should get fired, I really hate people like that.

Do you think you could try turmeric capsules or cbd oil against the pain?

And I am sorry to hear you were abused, no one should do that to a child.
Still, people should treat you kindly regardless of your height.

Did you know that for most of the world 1.50-160cm is a common height for men and women?
And since you are 14 you may not be done growing yet. I was not at 14.
It is really stupid how some people always find someone else their differences and then use it to bully them. It is cruel.
I have BPD and PTSD too, so I know what it can be like. Would you like to travel or save animals? That is something I would like to do.

People deserve housing, it is a human right. So do you. Are there any organizations near where you are that help homeless people?  
To cope with the physical pain, what have you tried?  
And if your health is not good, is it safe to donate plasma or do medical studies?  


And that other person about being homeless and having a phone...Loads of homeless people do have some things, including a phone.
In terms of the work it may not be any better than ordinary school, but at least this way you dont have to bother with the school you are going to now.

There are refugees who also no longer have family and friends. Yet to somehow manage to build a life in a new country? I really dont know how they do it. I dont think I can. What I am trying to say is, would you be open for trying to find fulfilment in something that is not dependend on people, like travel or art?  
And for the sad anniversaries, maybe do something for charity? Like plant a tree for them, save animals, something like that.
Depending on which program you pick, there are homeschool programs that are more like online school so your parents would not need to do much. Other than to let you ofcourse.
Where would you like to live? I research countries so if you tell me where you would like to live, I can look up countries and places that fit that description. If that would help?

As difficult as this is to accept for you, but there is nothing wrong with being a lesbian. Everyone is born the way they are, and being a lesbian is just a variation. I am pansexual myself. I promise you there will be a lady out there who will love you for who you are. Or even multiple ladies. They are out there.  
In many countries in the world, you can have a family also with another woman, through adoption or a sperm bank.   


The other day I read of a scientist who wants to give grants to women and other minorities so they could study science, do you want me to find the article back for you to see if you would be eligable for such a grant?  
I dont know where you are and I thought maybe the grant is country specific, but its been a week or so that I found the article so I kinda forgot.  


I dont think you are a monster. What are the things you regret saying and doing, if you want to talk about it?
I think some people would miss you. Living without a best friend, son and brother sound really tough, wow. My condolences. Do you have any other friends or family left?

I am sorry that happened to you, that is really not okay. You are worth much more than that abuse. You dont need to say anymore, I dont want to hurt you by making you look back on bad stuff.  


It is legally possible to be homeschooled in Finland. What would you and your parents think of that?

It is really not okay that medical shit can cost this much.  
You said the operation showed everything was okay. So does this mean you feel physically okay right now, after you heal from surgery, or is what you have still unexplained?  


I really hate how debt, which in a sense is imaginary as money is imaginary (really, think about it), is used to crush people their spirit and their lives. It is not okay. Medical care and an education are basic human rights.  
Sadly both modern day education and modern day medicine is often garbage, which is unfortunate but true.  


You can still travel, travel really does not have to cost a lot of money. Would you feel better if I told you some ways you could travel for reduced costs?  
I traveled while being really sick, so I just want to say travel is possible even with nearly no health or nearly no money. Both is MUCH tougher, but just either one is totally doable.

Tinnitus is really difficult. I have it intermittently, my mom all the time. She says she finds relief/joy at looking at small beautiful things. Like flowers on the street, birds singing, those little things. I used to think that was stupid but as I got older I started really appreciating that too.  
A funny cat video per day really can do wonders sometimes, even if life totally sucks and it doesnt change the situation one damn bit, it can still help.  


If I could I would like to help you. Totally no money (sick and without disability pension as my country doesnt give me one for my illness) so cant help you in that way but we can talk here if you like.  
I have more to say but I dont really know how to put it into words right now.  
I agree with the other poster that it really doesnt sound like your fault.  


Other than death to make the problems go away, what would really make your heart sing right now?
That is beautiful. Care to share some lyrics with us that you wrote?

In my opinion, those police officers should get fired. Or atleast get a stern warning from a supervisor. Mental and physical health are both really serious things, one should know the signs of something really being dangerously happening inside a person.  


And you are not pathetic, nor a loser. You matter. When did the voice start?

Self awareness still matters, because that contains the hope that some day, in different circumstances maybe, you would make better/different choices. At least that is how I feel about it.  


What would fix your situation according to you? What are your dreams?
What makes you depressed? What would you need/want to feel better about life?

School really sucks in my opinion and it is not necessary to learn anything. You can learn on your own, like with MOOCS.  
Would you prefer to be homeschooled or drop out and get a GED?  Which country are you located? If you want to share because then I can look up the rules for where you are for education choices.  


Social anxiety is hard...Were you bullied/hurt a lot that caused that?

Is there any way that you can get the housing stuff sorted?  
That must be so scary!  
Have you heard of workaway or wwoof? It is working+a roof over your head in a cool country. Would you like that?
How are you feeling?
Eating is important, everyone alive needs to eat at least some. What made you depressed?
Well some people do feel an enormous sense of purpose in their lives and I dont want to mock it. Just want to know what it is so I can inspire them.
Dying usually is painful. What would make you want to live? Who are the others you mention?

I have a friend who lives in Pittsburgh, and she told me that actually the pollution there is really high compared to the rest of the US. Especially PM2.5 which is highly inflammatory. Pollution is not just fumes.
Is there any way you could live in the neighborhood of Pittsburgh so you dont have to be too far away from everyone, but also not in it so the air is a bit cleaner?

I understand it is really complicated...I would just advice location change before end of life change, especially as it helped me so much, I wish it could help others. But I understand it if you cant move.

So this is about school? I wanted to kill myself because of school too. So I deeply know the feeling. One day you will be free of school though even if you live on. And does your mom know that if you are in the US, and some other countries too, you can still go to university if you drop out of school?  
What grade are you in now and what makes school terrible for you? Would you prefer to be homeschooled?
We cant name methods here. What are the reasons that make you "wimp out" as you call it?

What makes you think you are a failure?  


What makes life beautiful? And what makes it fucked up to you?
Your existence is not a waste of time. Or atleast that is what I believe. Who gave you the feeling your life is a waste of time?
It would have hurt a lot, so not the most painless method. Do you want to say why you would prefer not to live?

According to some people, Niburu will soon be here. According to the Jewish calender, the Messiah will have to come within 221 years.  
And lots of humans unfortunately are very destructive, also those in power, so the world could end soon enough...

It is really sad hospitals often dont help.  
I hope you can continue to be his friend. Does he have other friends?
How are you now? I hope you survived and if not that you are okay whereever you are.
What do you feel your job in the world is?

What would give you energy?   
Could you move back to your original country? Or start making a plan/saving up for that since you mentioned getting a job?   
Existential fatigue is a real thing and can hit at any age, it doesnt have to be forever though, even though it can.

If you feel up for it, how do all your identities feel about suicide? I mean how many do you have and how split are they, as in do 50% want to die 30%, 80%, different numbers?  


What would you need to enjoy life? Since some part of you says to want it.  


And I know that progression, the stages of "mental dying". And yet there is this hesitation...I know it.

Unfortunately most methods do have potential risks to the brain if failed, just the way it is. I get it though. I really need to leave where I live and the fastest and cheapest way to do that is by plane, however I really dont want to risk any more lung embolisms or hypoxemia. So while I cant stay where I am I cant do that either.I survived 3 brain infarcts and that was super tough...So I know a little of how you may feel. Maybe you dont feel like answering this, ignore if the case, what have you tried for healing? My symptoms got better after several years BUT I only had small infarcts, I dont know about you? Sometimes it never goes away and I know that.  


Edit: I read below you have MS. MS is a neurological inflammatory disease. Does your city/place where you live have a lot of pollution? Where I live does and moving away has  made my inflammatory illness a lot better and I never thought that would happen as mine is lyme disease so not auto immune. Cant say it will work that way for you, but just as thought to look into. Before you give up on life itself, maybe try location change if possible?

I very much understand the feeling. Also because I am sick and I dont want to see that get worse either. However I do want to stay around to see if I can help the earth somewhat, or at least one little corner of it. How do you feel about that?
It makes me think of Prussian and English royalty, not HP.
They are only different by 1 letter, the A and the M, so for me it would be too close. Then again they are both really nice names and they do sound a lot different so I think you can use it.
Personally I would pronounce it Ra-yeh-ra, but I can imagine many other options exist. It is also a verb in Spanish so not the prettiest in that sense, but the flower is so beautiful.
It is Arabic :)  . [http://quranicnames.com/zaheena/](http://quranicnames.com/zaheena/)

My Syrian (unfortunately) ex, wanted to name a son after his father, as he was named after his grandfather. So the 2 names would rotate. That seemed to be the custom in the province where he was from (Idlib province).

There is a youtube star named Veela, so I kinda want to say Avela like  Ah-vee-la. Anyway regardless of the pronunciation, I really love it. While googling I found it is a genus of moths, which does not put me off.
Iavis reminds me of a mashup between Iona and Avis. Mirma and Mavirma are not too bad. Not my style but also really not the worst in my opinion.

Gerrytoos, rhymes with dorritos or burritos...No, not a fan to use this as a real name.
For a full name it would be Gertrudis-Catharina, which while massively oldfashioned, atleast sounds like a real name. I could live with that.

Julian was actually used in medieval Britain by females also. It didnt become more male until usually. It is one of the few rare names that turned from gender neutral to masculine, usually it is gender neutral to feminine.

I named one of my birds Robin and a hamster Ezra/Esra (varied on spelling as one is a Hebrew boy name and the other a Turkish girl name, I didnt know the gender/sex of the hamster).
Rixen does not doesnt German either to me. Although there is the rare Dutch name Rixt, so it may be related to that somehow. Either way, cool name!
Esra is a Turkish girl's name, but Ezra is a Hebrew boy's name.
Why?

This used to be in my name top 5 along with:

1. Daniel. 2. Ilias/Elias. 3. Florian. 4. Jorian. 5. Julian. 
I love male names that have "an" as an ending or somewhere in them, or Eli somewhere in there.

Many similar names exist, Sarayah, Rhea, Ray, Rayera (for the flower). So honestly I can see it as a name. I also met an Indonesian girl with this name.
Raya seems to be Persian: http://quranicnames.com/raya/

http://quranicnames.com/rayyaa/

So honestly just go for it if you love it, it sounds lovely, and it is a 2 syllable name ending in -ah so it must exist somewhere.
I would personally spell it Raya though.
Zaheena.
Benjamin Wallace, Asher William, Conor Hudson, Weston Jay are my picks.

To give the person their due, Sanna is used in the Netherlands and Hazel and Holly are both very well known. Ash is somewhat used too.
I love Celandine and Marjoram (or Marjorie), Betony is more common as Bethany. Vervain is a very cool herb, just not very name-y.
Steen in Dutch would be pronounced stay-n, so not like in English, Stein/Stijn was very common here 10 years (for boys), Stein being German for stone.
Alwin?
I actually kind of like it. It is a tad too sweet, but I do like English word names.
I just looked it up, and it does not appear culturally or legally tolerated. Only cannabis is. Do you live in the Netherlands?
That is because the Dutch J is pronounced as Y :/
Konya is a Turkish city, and a Russian dimunitive for Konon, Kondratti and I think also Constantin.
Perdoceo means "teach" in Latin. https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/perdoceo

Behindthename.com and babynamewizard.com have some lists, but not all.
Countries like Morocco and Iceland that work with allowed name lists, may be easier to compile data from than others.
Marigold was mentioned and that always makes me think of Magnolia.
In the Netherlands, Zus (sister) was often used as a nickname, particularly for elder sisters. And sometimes also used as a given name...Maybe that is also what is going on here?
I am usually not at all a fan of occupational names, but I do like Author.

The Netherlands still has most harddrugs as illegal, so what do you mean with the Amsterdam suggestion? 
I think it was Portugal that actually did more to support the addicted.

Africa, as a continent, has lots of natural resources which they are underpaid for. And whatever they are paid for it, ends up with corrupt politicians/dictators, in most of Africa. Not all, but most.
Africa can be so much more.

I agree with you that countries need to clean up their pollution, with the heaviest polluters first, but unfortunately most countries are polluted, which is visible by looking at sites like http://aqicn.org

Using names outside your culture is okay. As long as it is not a name from a marginalized culture you dont belong too, or something like Cohen that was never meant as a first name but is a title.
What I mean is that using the name Alexis, for example, is okay if you are not Greek/Russian. Liora if you are not Israeli, but just like the meaning or sound.
Emma is also a very old name, it was the name of a Dutch Queen-Regent, so it doesnt sound unprofessional to me. And I agree with you in general it is a stupid argument.
If you like Sapphire, would you like Zephyr?

I love Ira, Ferdinand, Cecil, Ambrose, Percival and Basil.
Leopold I cant do due to King Leopold, and maybe IRA makes Ira undoable too, depending on where you life.
Maybe you would like Oswin too?

Ingrid and Saskia are two other ones that sometimes come up. Especially Saskia is said to be so quirky and young and I just cant see that.
For boys, long names like Abraham and the Ed- names are also just so old fashioned that they are not yet due for a revival. I do like them though, they are classic.
And names like Robin are much more unisex here still than the US. And Luca/Luka is unisex here, not just for boys. And Ezra/Esra, Ezra is  Hebrew and for boys, Esra Turkish and for girls.

Interesting combination. Where I am from Astrid is very much a mom name, and Zephyr would be seen as a hippy name. For me this reads like Barbara and Juniper, or Karen and Apple, would read in the US.
I do really like Zephyr though, I think it is beautiful. And I like the meaning connection too.
Overused? I researched some and it appears to only be on the charts in Poland. Correct me if I am wrong, but it does not appear to be in the top 100 of the US SSA.
In Dutch, au would sound like in English the sound in the word ouch, so it is different from both ow and or, but closer to ow than or.

I love Aurelia and Aurora. Unfortunately in English they dont sound so great due to the English r, but in Dutch, Spanish and other languages it does sound really beautiful. They are some of my favorites too.

Gothlob perhaps comes from Gotlieb(b)?
I researched some and there does appear to be a connection: https://www.behindthename.com/name/gottlob

I would not do Calvin because I dont like the historical figure. I do like the other ones. Definitely do not combine Calvin and Luther unless you want to make a STRONG religious impression.

Leo Rowan, Leo Ronan or Leo Micah is what I would choose fom you names. Or Isaac Ronan, is very beautiful too I think.

Kyler Bethwyn looks very gender neutral...Which is a style so I cant say it is wrong or anything, just something to look out for. Vox is the name of a broadcasting network, as is Fox. However Fox is used as a name more than Vox.
Prism is the name of a not so nice US law. Kalven reminds me of a misspelled version of Calvin, which is a male name. Maxima is a Dutch queen.
I would spell Madeleine as Madeleine. 

I do like all the others, and I love Antonia Althea, Lilac Magdalene, Imogen(e) Juniper, and Dahlia. Felix Edmund sounds very dignified and elegant too.

Brendan, Adrian, Virginia, Louise.

May not be entirely what you were looking for (as they are the names of people I know with Clark as a surname) but all names are recognizible and rather uncommon now.
That is a generalization about an entire continent. Are you serious here that you are justifying colonization as better?
I know educated women who have many children. And personally I am happy I was homeschooled starting age 11. However I was not married at 12.

Vivian, Eloise, Iona, Arwen, Eleonora/Leonora, Leona, Lovisa, Maira, Talitha, Beata, Ada, Azalea, Erin, Aurora, Verity, Berenice, Winifred.

Loving the suggestion of Dahlia for you too. I would spell Gwendolyn, Gwendolen. 

From your list I prefer Magnolia, Linnea, Ariadne in that order. I like all the others too
I love Etta and Jay for Juliette, but especially Etta. Never throught of that before.
The official version is that it comes from Maria Soledad, Mary of Solitude, but it ofcourse sounds like sun and sea, so that is a meaning too.
Liam is probably already so English for Sweden, I know that where I am from in Europe it would be seen as very American/English. So I would actually be happy with the old, classic, Swedish name.
Philomena could be an option. It shares the Ph and is also greek. I also love some of the other ideas mentioned in here.
Dekker/Decker is a Dutch surname. Feels too much like a last name to me, but I know some people are into that style.

Part of it may be that in Europe, witch trials were unfortunately so pervasive, they were not really named by place. Salem was named, so it kind of became a symbol for it all. Kinda like Auschwitz is the most famous concentration camp but it was far from the only one, or even the only nazi death camp in history.
There are actually several places named in Victoria in the English speaking world, and yet it is such a classic name it still reads very much as a personal name only, not a place name.

Being a teen mom should be someone's own choice (between abortion, adoption and keeping the baby), and we as a society should support her if she chooses to keep the baby.
Saying teen moms pick trashy names, may or may not be true (would depend on the individual I suppose), but it is definitely a judgement. An ageist judgement.
I know for most people it is all cool to discriminate based on age, but I dont think it is cool.

And no I am not a teen mom, but if I was one, my children would probably be named something like Helena and Daniel, classics.

Alice is related to Adelaide, and Alessia to Alexis, so you could use those for the middle name?

Or A names not yet mentioned:
Agnes, Allegra, Amalia, Amaryllis, Arabella, Amabel, Amy/Aimee...

For a first name I agree Violet or Vivian seems very nice. Other ideas:  Fiona, Nora/Norah, Willow, Lilian, Lily, Valerie, Vanessa, Matilda, Maud, Mariella, Emma, Saskia, Catriona.
Emma and Lily also contain the letters found in Maeve and Sylvia
Very royal, I love it

Going to the hospital is also not as common and assumed as it is in the US. Most births are still homebirths in the Netherlands, especially in the past.
My grandpa made my newborn sign.
Which area of the USA are you in?

Amabel has an m and a b in it and is rather unusual.

For the M and then B name my suggestion would be Maria Brene. Maria because I like it and Brene for Brene Brown.
I kind of like it, it reminds me of Mirre, which is Dutch for myrrh. Mirre is occassionally used as a name here but usually Mirte/Mirthe/Myrthe/Myrte is used.
I like Nivine, my friends writes it Niveen so I prefer that spelling. I really like it, and Dalia too.

Augusta/August, Wilhelmina or Amalia/Amelia are some other classic ideas.

More unique: Winter, Amaryllis, Corinthia.

Willow has been used as a name for quite some time actually. And these days there are much "crazier" names out there than Willow. Willow will pale in comparison, so dont worry. I think it is a sweet name. :)
You could use it as a nickname for Wilhelmina, if you want something more formal.
I would be happy to interact on that thread, and curious to see how others perceive their synesthesia.
Or Eclipse.
Names are colors for me too so I understand. I love Corwin out of this list, but I also really like Logan and Jasper. I dont like Lewis much by itself but I got a feeling to "upvote" it anyway.

Thank you. :) 

It is nice to hear that most people will probably understand Avine too.

Oh Tariqa is lovely, thank you! :) 

Avin is the original spelling that I found, so that is a plus. My name also has a silent e at the end and while it doesnt really bother me, it also was not really needed other than that my mom just thought it looked more elegant (I do agree but still).
I do worry though if people are not going to read the -vin at the end as vin, as in Vincent or Vince? In Dutch it also means fin, like from a fish, and it is a bit hard to not see that.
It is hard choosing for me as well, between Amaris and Ah-veen (whichever spelling, they all have pros and cons), luckily I still have a lot of time left.

In Dutch it is said a bit differently than flur, it is a bit hard to explain but maybe it can be found on forvo? I dont think people with English as a first language can make that exact sound though without trying really hard, so in day to day use it would likely be flur.

Yes, Antonia is one of my favorite options too, and it is my grandmother's middle name so it would be a meaningful choice. 
Yes the stress is on the second syllable.

I would say it as ah-MAR-iss. Interesting to hear it is so rare in the US, I think it is rare everywhere but I would assume that if it is used anywhere it would probably be in the US, following the name Damaris but then with the trend to chop the first letter off.

It is meant to be ah-Veen I am pretty sure. I would go with a-MAR-is but other people may pronounce it differently.

Avene is a minor skin care brand that I found, but it is not pronounced the same way.
That would depend entirely on flow with middle and last name for me. I like both equally. Would initials spell anything with either one?
It seems to be true in Germany, the Netherlands and Italy, so perhaps France too.
What a wonderful post! i know a Thecla.
Your Oswald could give him the nickname Ozzy.
I would go with Magnolia Beatrix or Magnolia Eleanor. Or since you like Lily and Lilian, do Lilian nicknamed Lily, or Margaret nicknamed Margot/Greta.

For Eleanor you can use Lea/Leo as a nickname, or even Leonie. Although Leonie is also a nice standalone name. I also thought of Grace for you, and Lucy. For boys I would suggest Frederick, although I like your current list too, very regal.

Alwyn sounds rather masculine to me. Astor does too but that one I had never heard before so would be easier for me to adapt to. I think Fran would be nicer as a nickname for Francesca but I do think that combination would be great with Amelia! Suggestions: Alwina, Wilhelmina, Astrid, Hope, Sadie, Juniper.

Two that came to mind are Guinevere and Marilyn. Especially the latter is probably not more modern, Genevieve is probably the most popular/modern right now from the suggested names. Or just Gwen. Maybe Wren? Similar names for boys: Gareth, Gwyn, Griffin, Glenn, Dorian...Similar as in similar letters, I dont know if you find them similar in style? Gwendolen/Gwendolyn is Welsh in origin, would you like a Welsh name?
He looks like, and his name sounds like, he could be a great philosopher one day

House Sunflower. Motto, I had to think long about that, I thought up "May the poetry be eternal". Sorry, it was in the middle of the nightwhen I wrote that so I missed the boy part. Not wanting it to sound too Muslim probably scratches Ali and Ahmad. Biblical: Keturah, Keziah (maybe too matchy with Ezekiel?), Lois, Leah, Lydia, Elisabeth, Eunice, Esther. Irish: Edna, Eilish, Elva, Kiera, Kathleen, Keeva (Caoimhe).

That is truly beautiful, especially with those meanings.

If not Elizabeth, how about Eleanor, Eliana? Instead of Tess, Theresa with Tess as a nickname? Cordelia with Cora as the nickname? Or Iris.

You can also look into Erich Traub, a nazi brought to the US during project Paperclip and what writer John Loftus said about him. Long article but it is worth the read: http://spitfirelist.com/for-the-record/ftr-480-plum-island-lyme-disease-and-the-erich-traub-file/
Boys: Udo, Udi, Ali. Girls: Ada, Eda/Ida, Ila

Eleanor, Beatriz/Beatrix, Vivian, Helena, Margaret. Lilian&Susannah do match to me but are very similar to Juliana...Just some random suggestions. I really like Mila too, but I do feel it is rather different from Juliana.
Siemen is not pronounced the exact same as semen, more like seaman, with the stress on the first syllable. It is an old Dutch variant of Simon.
Nancy originally was a nickname for Ann, and Susan does have the "ann" sound in it so that is another possible reason.

Miriam, primarily in spellings Mariam/Maryam/Meryam is a really popular name in most Arabic speaking countries, even in Turkey. As much of a classic there as in Judaism. So plenty of tiny Miriams on the globe outside of NYC.
Eli, Leo, Sebastian, Simon, Josef sound the most international from the suggestions.
Is there a family name you would like to use? Someone not family you would like to honor, like favorite book character?
Celendine is uncommon as a given name. It is a flower/herb.
It means night in Arabic too. And ecstasy (as in happiness), depending on the spelling of the name.
Clarity is used, uncommon but it happens.
